blockers.description: Phase 5 round 9 returned 1 HIGH. The round-8 TRX regex fix, which I hand-authored, is too permissive: testName="[^"]*(name1|name2)[^"]*" combined with substring FullyQualifiedName~ filters means suffix-extended tests such as RunAsync_MetadataBearingImport_PersistsMetadata_Unrelated satisfy the gate. The reviewer confirmed with a synthetic TRX that both unrelated names produce failed_count=2.
blockers.workaround: Fix is fully specified: exact FullyQualifiedName=DeckFlow.Core.Tests.ArchidektDeckCacheSessionTests.<method> filters, one exact counter per fully qualified name plus a total, requiring first_failed=1, second_failed=1, total_failed=2. Dispatch to Codex rather than hand-editing.

decisions.decision: D-24 - each combo-badge transport keys for its own consumer
decisions.rationale: The AJAX DTO re-keys ComboBadgeByCardName onto raw pool names server-side under StringComparer.Ordinal; the Razor view model keeps normalized keys and normalizes at lookup. Ordinal rather than OrdinalIgnoreCase because cut-lab.ts reads these keys with case-sensitive JavaScript property lookup and CutLabStateSerializer does not canonicalize Pool. A TypeScript port of CardNormalizer.Normalize was considered and rejected: duplicating the star-strip, *f*-strip, DFC split and punctuation collapse in a second language with nothing binding them would silently recreate the defect class.

decisions.decision: Phase 4 scope widened to repair three pre-existing combo-badge readers
decisions.rationale: The plan had claimed twin evidence chips get badges for free. They never rendered at all: the dictionary is written normalized and read raw at CutLab.cshtml:708, cut-lab.ts:1446, and the card-text JSON builder at CutLab.cshtml:234-275. These were found in rounds 8, 9 and 10 respectively, because no consumer census was done before asserting the behavior worked.

CardTextByCardName is keyed OrdinalIgnoreCase but consumed by case-sensitive JavaScript, so two pool entries differing only by case lose one card-text entry. Same hazard as D-24, but pre-existing, built by two separate builders, and read server-side at CutLab.cshtml:237 - out of scope for this phase. Live follow-up count is now six.

decisions.decision: Phase 6 wave 1 superseded: per-endpoint throttle gates, not a 200ms restore
decisions.rationale: 500ms IS Scryfall's documented per-endpoint limit; the 200ms it replaced came from misreading the docs' all-other-methods row, and ScryfallThrottleTests.cs:174 pins >=450ms specifically to assert it. Recovering throughput legitimately means per-endpoint gate state, which requires threading an endpoint key through 14 call sites across 8 services.

decisions.decision: Phase 6 wave 2 scoped to SearchFallbackCardAsync only
decisions.rationale: SearchPrintingFallbackCardAsync is a three-stage progressive escalation under unique=prints with per-name best-match selection; batching it would redesign its matching semantics. Analysis and Deck History therefore get no request-count change this phase.

context_notes: Phase 4's plans needed TWELVE convergence rounds. The post-mortem produced four preventive rules, now in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md under 'Plan authoring: four rules that keep the review loop short' plus three project memory files. Dominant cause was serialized discovery of a three-reader production bug across rounds 8-12; second was that each fold added new unreviewed surface, so in rounds 9-11 every HIGH was a defect in the previous round's fix. Executing now is deliberate - converged plans decay against a moving codebase and this one agrees with HEAD as of 19fdce26. Phase 4 (DeckFlow.Web) and Phase 5 (DeckFlow.Core) have zero file overlap, so a read-only Phase 5 review can run concurrently with Phase 4 execution; two full-access Codex writers must never share this worktree. The untracked _edhrec-brackets/ and _role-floor-research/ directories must never be staged - always use explicit git add -- <paths>.
